name: Rename the design skill to spec

pr.title: Rename the design skill to spec
pr.head: 774c0b554a1425b9e617c8ab2d9ce06dcd42232f

summary: Projector's plugin gives Claude Code and Codex the same set of skills, written procedures an agent follows when the user invokes them by name. One of those skills writes a project's plan, the technical document under docs/projects/ that another person or agent implements later. Until this change, that skill was called design.

The name collides with Claude Code itself. On accounts whose organization enables Claude Design, a bare /design opens Claude Design's “Make a new Design artifact” command, so the skill is reachable there only by its namespaced form, /projector:design. This pull request renames the skill to spec, which names what the skill writes and which no Claude Code command or bundled skill uses.

The rename touches every place that names the skill: its folder and Codex interface file, the implement skill that points users at it, the packaging test that lists the published skills, the README, the plugin guide, two completed plans, and the marketing site. Prose that uses “design” in its ordinary sense stays, and so does the Codex manifest's example prompt, “Plan this project with Projector.”, which reaches the skill through its description rather than its name.

Once this merges and a user updates the plugin, /projector:spec and $spec invoke the skill, and /projector:design and $design no longer do. The skill's description still lists “design” among the requests it handles, so asking an agent to design a project still reaches it.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Skill: a folder under skills/ holding a SKILL.md. Its frontmatter name must match the folder name.
  • Plugin namespace: Claude Code invokes a plugin skill as /projector:<skill>, and also as a bare /<skill> when no built-in command has that name.
  • Codex invocation: Codex invokes the same skill as $<skill>, and reads its display name and default prompt from agents/openai.yaml inside the skill's folder.
  • Plan: a project's readme.md under docs/projects/, which this skill writes.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The Projector review of 774c0b5 is clean, with no finding threads. It suggests one change to the pull request body: the ## Testing section's git grep uses \b, which git's default extended regular expressions on macOS do not support, so its \$design\b alternative never matches there. A plain \$design search at this head finds nothing, so the body's claim holds.

groups.title: The skill moves to skills/spec
groups.kicker: The skill's folder, frontmatter, heading, Codex interface file, and the test that lists published skills.
intro: Both plugin manifests publish the whole skills/ folder, so a skill's name is its folder name. Moving skills/design to skills/spec is what renames the command. The frontmatter name and the heading follow the folder, and the Codex interface file moves with it, carrying a new display name and a $spec default prompt.

The packaging test is the only list of skill names in code. It checks that the folders under skills/ are exactly the published set and that each skill's frontmatter name matches its folder, so a half-done rename fails it.

checks.text: At this head, git grep finds no `design`, $design, projector:design, skills/design, “design skill”, or “Design a project” anywhere in the repository. Neither marketplace file, nor any code under src/, .github/, or install.sh, names a skill folder.

files.note: The skill itself, moved from skills/design/SKILL.md. Only the frontmatter, the heading, and the opening paragraph change.

checks.text: The description still lists “design” among the requests the skill handles, beside the new “specify”. An agent picks a skill from its description, so a user who asks to design a project still reaches this one. Line 18's “Do not design from the request alone” uses the word in its ordinary sense and stays.

files.note: Codex's interface file for the old name, deleted. Its replacement is the next file.
The same interface file under the new folder, with display_name Spec and a $spec default prompt. It has the same shape as the files beside implement, finish, and write.
The published skill set names spec instead of design.

checks.text: The full suite runs 442 tests OK at this head, with one skip, the compiled-script check that needs npm ci in site/. The packaging tests among them confirm that the folders under skills/ match this set and that skills/spec/SKILL.md declares name: spec. claude plugin validate . and claude plugin validate skills both pass.

groups.title: Skills and documents that name it
groups.kicker: The implement skill, the README, the plugin guide, and two completed plans.
intro: Each of these files names the skill, and each edit swaps the name and nothing else. The implement skill matters most, because it tells an agent to stop and suggest the planning skill when a described change is too big to build directly. It now suggests spec and says the work needs “a spec”.
The two plans, agent-instructions and projector, are both completed, so they make no readiness claim. Their edits make them name the skills that exist now.

files.note: Points users at spec for work that needs a plan first.

checks.text: This is the one instruction an agent acts on: when work spans several parts of the system, changes an interface, or leaves a product choice open, the agent stops and suggests spec. A stale name here would send users to a command that no longer exists.

files.note: The plugin guide's skill list, the skill's one-line description, and both invocation examples.

checks.text: The Claude Code 2.1.292 binary registers built-in commands named design and plan but none named spec, checked with strings on the installed binary. A bare /spec therefore reaches this skill, and the namespaced /projector:spec shown here always does.

files.note: The README's list of plugin skills.
A completed plan's list of skills whose validation step changed.
A completed plan's description of the planning skill.

groups.title: The marketing site
groups.kicker: The agents section's first step and its Codex line.
intro: The marketing site walks a reader through three steps, each with the command that runs it. The first step's title becomes “Spec a project”, its command becomes /projector:spec, and the Codex line below the steps names $spec. Only the three strings change, and the site's preview deployment for this head succeeded.

files.note: Three strings in the agents section: a step title, its command, and the Codex skill list.
